scenarios.purpose: Example manifest for the coverage-oracle validator; the bootstrap declares the repository phase at a unique anchor.
scenarios.rationale: Synthetic example that exercises the version-1 manifest shape and the anchor-resolution check.

scenarios.purpose: Read configured GitHub source material through the explicitly approved Octokit adapter.
scenarios.rationale: The approved live-read composition root uses official Octokit REST methods for the documented source-gathering workflow; tests inject a fake and never execute the calls.

scenarios.purpose: Publish an explicitly confirmed GitHub release through the isolated write adapter.
scenarios.rationale: The isolated Octokit writer performs the documented authorization, reconciliation, and confirmed release mutation calls; tests inject a fake and never execute them.

scenarios.purpose: Draft a structured, source-grounded release body through the isolated OpenAI Responses adapter.
scenarios.rationale: The explicit live-AI composition root uses the official Responses SDK method with a strict schema and disabled storage; tests inject a fake and never execute the call.

scenarios.purpose: Review or produce an alternate structured release draft through the isolated Anthropic Messages adapter.
scenarios.rationale: The explicit live-AI composition root uses the official Messages SDK method with structured json_schema output; tests inject a fake and never execute the call.

scenarios.purpose: Synchronize sponsor-tier products and prices and create hosted Checkout and billing-portal sessions through the isolated Stripe adapter.
scenarios.rationale: The explicit live-billing composition root uses official product, price, Checkout, and billing-portal SDK methods with per-resource idempotency keys and reuses matching resources instead of mutating an active price; tests inject a fake and never execute the calls.

scenarios.purpose: Verify a Stripe webhook's signature against the raw request body before any parsing, then project the limited subscription events that affect sponsor membership.
scenarios.rationale: The official Stripe SDK signature-verification method runs entirely offline against bytes already received; only a signature-verified event of a documented type is mapped and projected, deduplicated by event id plus payload hash. Tests use generateTestHeaderString to sign fixtures locally and never send or receive network traffic.

scenarios.purpose: Isolate a maintainer CLI shape that reads a comparison range through a function-local, directly constructed Octokit client rather than Release Relay's injected read adapter.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises a direct-construction client shape distinct from packages/github-integration/src/live.ts's injected adapter; the code never runs and the token is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: Isolate a maintainer helper that prepares a create-release call through a class-held Octokit client field, varying the client-construction shape from the other atomic GitHub scenarios and the product adapter.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises the class-field client-construction shape; the call is only ever prepared, never sent, and the workspace has no runtime script or test that invokes it.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate same-provider negative: real GitHub SDK usage for an operation outside Release Relay's documented product workflow, so it is not conflated with the release-publication call site.
scenarios.rationale: This call is genuine, correctly attributed GitHub SDK evidence, but it is deliberately unrelated to any Release Relay product operation (repository identity, comparisons, pull requests, issues, contributors, releases, or the confirmed release write), so it is reviewed at supporting rather than alertable confidence to keep the alertable band reserved for product-critical call sites.

scenarios.purpose: Isolate a maintainer tool that drafts a short release-note summary through a direct Responses client with bounded structured input, rather than through Release Relay's injected drafting adapter.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises a direct-construction Responses client shape distinct from packages/openai-integration/src/draft.ts's injected adapter, using the same product-plausible literal model identifier as its tests; the code never runs and the API key is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate same-provider negative: real OpenAI SDK usage for a different supported operation outside Release Relay's documented product workflow, so it is not conflated with the release-drafting call site.
scenarios.rationale: This call is genuine, correctly attributed OpenAI SDK evidence for a real embeddings-search maintainer utility, but it is deliberately unrelated to the structured, source-grounded release draft that is Release Relay's documented OpenAI product operation, so it is reviewed at supporting rather than alertable confidence to keep the alertable band reserved for the product-critical call site.

scenarios.purpose: Isolate a maintainer tool that reviews a short release-note summary through a direct Messages client with a narrow input, rather than through Release Relay's injected review adapter.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises a direct-construction Messages client shape distinct from packages/anthropic-integration/src/review.ts's injected adapter, using the same product-plausible literal model identifier as its tests; the code never runs and the API key is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate same-provider negative: real Anthropic SDK usage for a different supported operation outside Release Relay's documented product workflow, so it is not conflated with the draft-review call site.
scenarios.rationale: This call is genuine, correctly attributed Anthropic SDK evidence for a real token-budget-estimation maintainer utility, but it is deliberately unrelated to the structured draft review or alternate draft that is Release Relay's documented Anthropic product operation, so it is reviewed at supporting rather than alertable confidence to keep the alertable band reserved for the product-critical call site.

scenarios.purpose: Isolate a maintainer helper that creates a sponsor Checkout Session through a factory-constructed, API-version-pinned client, rather than through Release Relay's injected billing adapter.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises a factory-construction client shape distinct from packages/stripe-integration/src/billing.ts's injected adapter, and deliberately pins an explicit apiVersion where the product adapter pins only the host, so both dimensions have reviewed coverage; the code never runs and the secret key is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: Isolate a maintainer helper that creates a sponsor billing-portal session through a dependency-injected client field, varying the client-construction shape from the other atomic Stripe scenarios and the product adapter.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises the dependency-injection client-construction shape; the code never runs and the workspace is never given a real client.

scenarios.purpose: Isolate a minimal browser hand-off to a server-prepared, hosted sponsor Checkout Session using the official browser Stripe.js SDK, handling only publishable configuration and never card data.
scenarios.rationale: The browser Stripe.js load call confirms the client environment is ready before handing off to the hosted Checkout URL the server already prepared; the redirect itself is an injected callback so this workspace has no DOM library dependency, and the publishable key is an explicit parameter and an unmistakably fake structural value, never a real credential. The code never runs.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate same-provider negative: real Stripe SDK usage for an operation outside Release Relay's documented product workflow, so it is not conflated with the sponsor-billing call sites.
scenarios.rationale: This call is genuine, correctly attributed Stripe SDK evidence for a real account-balance maintainer utility, but it is deliberately unrelated to sponsor-tier products and prices, Checkout, the billing portal, and signed webhooks, which are Release Relay's documented Stripe product operations, so it is reviewed at supporting rather than alertable confidence to keep the alertable band reserved for product-critical call sites.

scenarios.purpose: Read the comparison range for an upcoming release through a cached singleton client constructed in the same module, inside the composed deployment.
scenarios.rationale: The composed deployment's source-gathering module constructs a cached singleton client on first use and reads the documented comparison range in the same file that owns construction; the local binding deliberately reuses the `client` name also bound in the drafting module and the sponsor-portal class, so the no-observation expectation pins that the reused name does not leak the drafting call site across files. The workspace compiles only and the token is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: Draft the release body through a default-exported drafting function that unwraps its optional client with a non-null wrapper, inside the composed deployment.
scenarios.rationale: The drafting module is consumed through its default export, constructs its own Responses client from an explicit key parameter, and reaches it through a non-null wrapper that fails loudly on missing configuration before any request is prepared; the local binding reuses the `client` name also bound in the source-gathering module, so the no-observation expectation pins that no GitHub comparison call is attributed to this file. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: Review the release draft through a dependency-injected Messages client reached by bracket access, inside the composed deployment.
scenarios.rationale: The review module owns no construction: the composition root at scenarios/composed/relay-deployment/src/relay.ts constructs the Messages client and injects it as the `api` parameter, and the call site reaches the messages namespace through bracket access to vary the call-expression shape from the dot-access forms elsewhere. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: Open a sponsor billing-portal session through a class-held client field reached from an arrow-function class property, inside the composed deployment.
scenarios.rationale: The sponsor-portal module owns no construction: the composition root at scenarios/composed/relay-deployment/src/relay.ts constructs the Stripe client and injects it into the class field, and the portal entry point is an arrow-function property that reads the class-held client through `this`, exercising the arrow-function class-access shape at the actual call site. The workspace compiles only and is never given a real client.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate composed-deployment negative: a narrow internal fetch wrapper whose generic `http` name is reused across files, with no provider import or call, expecting no provider attribution.
scenarios.rationale: The internal HTTP wrapper only fetches deployment-internal status endpoints and its `http` name is one of the generic names deliberately reused across the composed deployment; the file contains no provider import, client, or call, so the reviewed expectation is that none of the deployment's four provider call sites is attributed to it. The workspace compiles only and the fetch target is an explicit parameter, never a provider host.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate composed-deployment negative: an internal status reader whose `api` record reuses the name bound to provider clients in other files, expecting no cross-file provider attribution.
scenarios.rationale: The internal status reader wraps the plain internal fetch helper in an `api` record whose name is deliberately reused from the review module's injected provider parameter and the drafting module's unwrapped client binding; nothing in this file constructs or calls a provider client, so the reviewed expectation is that neither provider call site leaks onto the reused name across files. The workspace compiles only and the status path is deployment-internal.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate composed-deployment negative: an ordinary function retained from a pre-class refactor, invoked with a rebound `this` whose `client` field is a display label rather than the class-held provider client.
scenarios.rationale: The legacy announcement function is an ordinary function invoked only through .call with a plain record whose `client` field is a display label string, so the `this.client` access can never reach the provider client held by the real sponsor-portal class; the reviewed expectation pins that no class-field name reuse or cross-class leakage attributes the billing-portal call site to this file. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: Draft a short release body through a raw Responses endpoint request addressed by its full fixed URL, rather than through the SDK.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises the full-URL raw HTTP call shape against the documented drafting endpoint, distinct from the SDK call sites; the request can never execute, the input is inert fixed text, and the API key is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: Review a short release summary through a raw Messages endpoint request assembled from a fixed base host plus a path suffix.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises the base-plus-path raw HTTP call shape against the documented review endpoint, with the version header matching the value the installed SDK itself sends; the request can never execute, the input is an inert summary, and the API key is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: Open a sponsor billing-portal session through a raw Stripe endpoint request addressed by a template literal over a fixed base host.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises the template-literal raw HTTP call shape against the documented billing-portal endpoint with form encoding; the request can never execute, the customer and return URL are inert structural examples, and the secret key is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: Read a comparison range through a narrow local fetch wrapper that applies GitHub REST conventions, rather than through the SDK.
scenarios.rationale: A small, reviewed, compile-only workspace exercises the narrow-wrapper raw HTTP call shape: the provider evidence sits at the actual call inside the wrapper while the resource path is assembled at the caller; the request can never execute and the token is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate unrelated-provider control: a real Slack chat.postMessage call that must not be attributed to any supported provider.
scenarios.rationale: The usage is genuine and correctly Slack's own HTTP API with a bearer token, but no supported provider SDK, client, host, or call exists in this file, so none of the product call sites may be attributed to it. The workspace compiles only and the bot token is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate unrelated-provider control: a real Twilio Messages API call that must not be attributed to any supported provider.
scenarios.rationale: The usage is genuine and correctly Twilio's own HTTP API with basic auth over an accounts path, but no supported provider SDK, client, host, or call exists in this file, so none of the product call sites may be attributed to it. The workspace compiles only and the credentials are explicit parameters, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate unrelated-provider control: a real S3 object-URL builder that must not be attributed to any supported provider.
scenarios.rationale: The helper formats a genuine S3 object URL from an explicit bucket, key, and fixed region, but it issues no request and no supported provider SDK, client, host, or call exists in this file, so none of the product call sites may be attributed to it. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate unrelated-provider control: a real Discord webhook announcement that must not be attributed to any supported provider.
scenarios.rationale: The usage is genuine and correctly Discord's own webhook API, but no supported provider SDK, client, host, or call exists in this file, so none of the product call sites may be attributed to it. The workspace compiles only and the webhook credentials are explicit parameters, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate local-name control: display-model classes that reuse the provider class names without any provider import, client, or endpoint.
scenarios.rationale: The classes are local UI badge models whose names coincide with provider class names, but the file imports no provider SDK, constructs no client, and names no provider endpoint, so no provider observation may be attributed to it. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate lookup-table control: endpoint-looking strings in a pure routing-data file that never issues a request.
scenarios.rationale: The catalog is documentation and allowlist data containing provider endpoint strings, but a data literal is not provider usage: no client is constructed and no request is issued, so no provider observation may be attributed to this file. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate shadowed-binding control: a real provider import referenced only in a type position, with its name shadowed by a plain local string.
scenarios.rationale: The type-only import is real but no client is constructed and no call is issued; the inner binding shadows the imported name with a version-label string, so a name-only match must not attribute the review call site to this file. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate dynamic-value control: a configuration-driven dispatcher whose eventual provider and identifier cannot be proven from source.
scenarios.rationale: The dispatch target is resolved at runtime from serialized configuration, so the source is intentionally insufficient for a deterministic conclusion about which provider, if any, the eventual call touches; the reviewed outcome is explicit uncertainty, which must not be collapsed into a confident negative. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate foreign-host control: an internal gateway client whose paths resemble provider API paths but whose host is not a provider endpoint.
scenarios.rationale: The gateway fetches a private internal host and the path builders deliberately resemble provider API paths, but path shape alone without the provider host must not constitute provider usage, so neither the review nor the drafting call site may be attributed to this file. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate path-disposition control: real OpenAI SDK usage placed under a test path, expected to be demoted below the alertable band.
scenarios.rationale: The SDK usage is genuine and correctly attributed, but the source-path policy deliberately demotes test paths below the alertable band, so the reviewed expectation is a demoted observation rather than an alertable one. The workspace compiles only, no test runner executes this file, and the API key is an explicit parameter, never loaded from the environment.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate path-disposition control: real Stripe SDK usage placed under a fixture path, expected to be demoted below the alertable band.
scenarios.rationale: The SDK usage is genuine and correctly attributed, but the source-path policy deliberately demotes fixture paths below the alertable band, so the reviewed expectation is a demoted observation rather than an alertable one. The workspace compiles only and is never invoked, the secret key is an explicit parameter, and the customer id and return URL are inert structural examples.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate path-disposition control: a generated file containing a provider-looking request, expected to be excluded from scanning by policy.
scenarios.rationale: The file is marked and placed as generated output and contains a provider-looking probe request that never executes, but the source-path policy deliberately excludes generated files from scanning entirely, so the reviewed expectation is a named file exclusion rather than any observation, positive or negative.

scenarios.purpose: A deliberate path-disposition control: a vendored legacy file containing a provider-looking request, expected to be excluded from scanning by policy.
scenarios.rationale: The file is vendored third-party code kept unmodified for reference and contains a provider-looking legacy request that never executes, but the source-path policy deliberately excludes vendored files from scanning entirely, so the reviewed expectation is a named file exclusion rather than any observation, positive or negative.
